claims.claim: In primary tumors, NAB2-STAT6 activates a neuroendocrine gene signature that sets it apart from most sarcomas.
claims.source: In primary tumors, NAB2-STAT6 activates a neuroendocrine gene signature that sets it apart from most sarcomas.
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq analysis of primary tumors (Figure 1) and comparison with TCGA database (Figure 6).

claims.claim: All eight primary SFT tumors shared one common NAB2-STAT6 isoform, spanning the first four exons of NAB2 and all but the first STAT6 exon.
claims.source: All tumors shared one common NAB2-STAT6 isoform, spanning the first four exons of NAB2 and all but the first STAT6 exon (Figure 1c, Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
claims.evidence: This is directly supported by fusion detection analysis using Arriba on RNA-seq data from the eight FFPE samples, as shown in Figure 1c.

claims.claim: IGF2 was the most upregulated gene in SFTs.
claims.source: Notably, the most upregulated gene was IGF2, an EGR1 target that was recognized as a major driver of a hypoglycemic condition occurring in <5% of SFTs (Doege-Potter syndrome).
claims.evidence: This is supported by differential gene expression analysis from RNA-seq of primary tumors versus normal tissue (Figure 1d).

claims.claim: Neuronal development programs are broadly upregulated in SFTs.
claims.source: Gene ontology and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed that neuronal development programs are broadly upregulated in SFTs (Figure 1e, Figure 1—figure supplement 1e).
claims.evidence: This is supported by GO and GSEA analysis of upregulated genes from RNA-seq data, as shown in Figure 1e.

claims.claim: Immune and cell signaling pathways are significantly downregulated in SFTs.
claims.source: Conversely, immune and cell signaling pathways are significantly downregulated (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d–e), suggesting that SFTs may be immunologically 'cold'.
claims.evidence: This is supported by GO and GSEA analysis of downregulated genes from RNA-seq data.

claims.claim: EGR1 binding motifs were the top enriched motifs at promoters of upregulated genes in SFTs.
claims.source: We found that binding sites for DB1, MAZ, MOVO−B, and EGR1 were the top enriched motifs by adjusted p-value and that EGR1 motifs were over-represented in the whole enrichment matrix (Figure 1f).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TRANSFAC motif analysis of promoter regions of upregulated genes, as shown in Figure 1f.

claims.claim: NAB2-STAT6 expression peaked at 48 hours of doxycycline treatment in U2OS cells.
claims.source: We observed expression of NAB2-STAT6 starting at 24 hr of doxycycline treatment, peaking at 48 hr (Figure 2a).
claims.evidence: This is directly shown by immunoblot analysis in Figure 2a.

claims.claim: 562 genes were upregulated after 48 hours of NAB2-STAT6 expression in U2OS cells.
claims.source: Larger scale gene expression changes were apparent after 48 hr of doxycycline with 562 upregulated genes (73%), including IGF2 and several neuronal regulators.
claims.evidence: This is supported by 3' mRNA QuantSeq analysis shown in Figure 2c.

claims.claim: About 27% of differentially expressed genes were downregulated after 48 hours of NAB2-STAT6 expression.
claims.source: About 27% of differentially expressed genes were downregulated (Figure 2c and Supplementary file 2), indicating that the primary function of NAB2-STAT6 may be transcriptional activation.
claims.evidence: This is supported by 3' mRNA QuantSeq analysis shown in Figure 2c and represents an inference about the primary function.

claims.claim: Promoters of upregulated genes in NAB2-STAT6 expressing cells were overwhelmingly enriched for EGR1 motifs.
claims.source: Promoters of upregulated genes were overwhelmingly enriched for EGR1 motifs, while STAT motifs were not significantly enriched (Figure 2e).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TRANSFAC motif analysis shown in Figure 2e.

claims.claim: STAT motifs were not significantly enriched at promoters of upregulated genes in NAB2-STAT6 expressing cells.
claims.source: Promoters of upregulated genes were overwhelmingly enriched for EGR1 motifs, while STAT motifs were not significantly enriched (Figure 2e).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TRANSFAC motif analysis shown in Figure 2e.

claims.claim: The expression of endogenous NAB2, NAB1, and EGR1 increased over time of doxycycline treatment.
claims.source: Interestingly, the expression of endogenous NAB2, NAB1, and EGR1 followed a similar trend, suggesting that the fusion protein enables a feed-forward mechanism of the EGR1 regulatory axis (Figure 2f).
claims.evidence: This is supported by normalized read counts from 3' mRNA QuantSeq shown in Figure 2f.

claims.claim: 1394 peaks gained significant NAB2-STAT6 signal after 48 hours of doxycycline in U2OS cells.
claims.source: We identified 1394 peaks that gained significant NAB2-STAT6 signal compared to day 0 and were almost equally distributed between promoters (57%) and distal cis-regulatory regions (43%, Figure 3a, Figure 3—figure supplement 1a, and Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq analysis of NAB2-STAT6 FLAG shown in Figure 3a.

claims.claim: NAB2-STAT6 peaks were almost equally distributed between promoters (57%) and distal cis-regulatory regions (43%).
claims.source: We identified 1394 peaks that gained significant NAB2-STAT6 signal compared to day 0 and were almost equally distributed between promoters (57%) and distal cis-regulatory regions (43%, Figure 3a, Figure 3—figure supplement 1a, and Supplementary file 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by genomic distribution analysis of ChIP-seq peaks shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a.

claims.claim: Endogenous EGR1 binding increased at least twofold at most NAB2-STAT6 sites upon NAB2-STAT6 expression.
claims.source: Next, we analyzed endogenous EGR1 at NAB2-STAT6 sites and found seeding binding across the vast majority of fusion protein peaks (Figure 3a). Upon NAB2-STAT6 expression, EGR1 binding increased at least twofold at most sites.
claims.evidence: This is supported by EGR1 ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 3a.

claims.claim: NAB2-STAT6 peaks were moderately accessible at day 0 and their accessibility increased twofold at 48 hours of doxycycline.
claims.source: We performed ATAC-seq to investigate chromatin accessibility status. NAB2-STAT6 peaks were moderately accessible at day 0 and their accessibility increased twofold (similar to EGR1 binding) at 48 hr of doxycycline (Figure 3a).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ATAC-seq analysis shown in Figure 3a.

claims.claim: Endogenous NAB2 localized at NAB2-STAT6 peaks but not STAT6 in control conditions.
claims.source: We next profiled endogenous NAB2 and STAT6 in control conditions and found that NAB2 localized at NAB2-STAT6 peaks but not STAT6 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq analysis of endogenous NAB2 and STAT6 in control U2OS cells shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claims.claim: NAB2-STAT6 did not bind any STAT6 control sites.
claims.source: Conversely, NAB2-STAT6 did not bind any STAT6 control sites (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1c.

claims.claim: Motif analysis of NAB2-STAT6 peaks identified a strong EGR1/EGR2 signature but no STAT family motifs.
claims.source: To further assess determinants of NAB2-STAT6 binding, we performed motif analysis using HOMER and identified a strong EGR1/EGR2 signature but no STAT family motifs (Figure 3b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by HOMER motif analysis shown in Figure 3b.

claims.claim: NAB2-STAT6 target genes were highly enriched in NAB2-STAT6 upregulated genes found by RNA-seq analysis.
claims.source: Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) showed that NAB2-STAT6 target genes, as determined by ChIP-seq, were highly enriched in NAB2-STAT6 upregulated genes found by RNA-seq analysis (Figure 3c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 3c, demonstrating correlation between binding and transcriptional activation.

claims.claim: 6284 NAB2 peaks, 1640 STAT6 peaks, and 38,036 RNAPII peaks were identified in primary tumor cells.
claims.source: We identified 6284 NAB2 peaks, 1640 STAT6 peaks, and 38,036 RNAPII peaks in primary tumor cells.
claims.evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq analysis of a primary SFT tumor shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: 718 putative NAB2-STAT6 binding sites were identified in primary tumor cells, 69% of which were distal to gene promoters.
claims.source: Peak overlap analysis revealed 718 putative NAB2-STAT6 binding sites, 69% of which were distal to gene promoters and likely to represent transcriptional enhancers (Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplement 1c and Supplementary file 4).
claims.evidence: This is supported by peak overlap analysis and genomic distribution analysis shown in Figure 4b and Figure 4—figure supplement 1c.

claims.claim: NAB2 only sites in primary tumors were enriched for EGR1/2 motifs.
claims.source: NAB2 only sites were enriched for EGR1/2 motifs (Figure 4c, Figure 4—figure supplement 1d) and the same motif profile was found at NAB2-STAT6 peaks (Figure 4c, Figure 4—figure supplement 1e).
claims.evidence: This is supported by HOMER motif analysis shown in Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 1d.

claims.claim: STAT6 only peaks in primary tumors were enriched for GRE and STAT motifs.
claims.source: STAT6 only peaks, instead, were enriched for GRE and STAT motifs (Figure 4c, Figure 4—figure supplement 1f).
claims.evidence: This is supported by HOMER motif analysis shown in Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 1f.

claims.claim: Genes nearest to NAB2-STAT6 peaks in primary tumors were significantly upregulated in SFTs.
claims.source: Gene set enrichment analysis of NAB2-STAT6 peaks (closest gene) showed significant correlation with upregulated genes in SFTs (Figure 4d).
claims.evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 4d.

claims.claim: There was limited overlap between NAB2-STAT6 sites in the primary tumor and those retrieved in U2OS.
claims.source: We found limited overlap between NAB2-STAT6 sites in the primary tumor and those retrieved in U2OS (Figure 4e-f, Figure 4—figure supplement 1g-h), consistent with the limited overlap between their transcriptomes.
claims.evidence: This is supported by comparison of ChIP-seq peaks between primary tumor and U2OS cells.

claims.claim: NAB1 and EGR1 were the top interactors of NAB2-STAT6 in nuclear extracts.
claims.source: Both antibodies efficiently immunoprecipitated the chimeric protein, as well as NAB1 and EGR1 (Figure 5a).
claims.evidence: This is supported by LC-MS/MS analysis of NAB2 and STAT6 immunoprecipitates shown in Figure 5a.

claims.claim: EGR1 co-purified along with CBP/P300 and RNAPII subunits upon NAB2-STAT6 expression.
claims.source: In addition, EGR1 co-purified along with CBP/P300 and RNAPII subunits suggesting that NAB2-STAT6 co-opts EGR1 co-activator functions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a).
claims.evidence: This is supported by LC-MS/MS analysis of EGR1 immunoprecipitates shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1a.

claims.claim: NAB1 is the strongest interactor of NAB2-STAT6 across multiple experiments.
claims.source: NAB1 is the strongest interactor of NAB2-STAT6 across multiple experiments (Figure 5—figure supplement 1d), suggesting that a heterodimeric form of the oncogenic protein may be its most common form.
claims.evidence: This is supported by multiple IP-MS experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1d.

claims.claim: The chimeric protein can heterodimerize with endogenous, full-length NAB2.
claims.source: Additionally, the chimeric protein can heterodimerize with endogenous, full-length NAB2 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1e–f).
claims.evidence: This is supported by peptide mapping from IP-MS experiments showing peptides unique to full-length NAB2, as shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1e-f.

claims.claim: NAB2-STAT6 was only present in the nuclear fraction of doxycycline-treated cells.
claims.source: Immunoblot analysis shows that NAB2-STAT6 was only present in the nuclear fraction of Dox conditions.
claims.evidence: This is supported by subcellular fractionation and immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 5b.

claims.claim: NAB2 and EGR1 were cytoplasmic in control conditions but became nuclear in doxycycline conditions.
claims.source: NAB2 and EGR1 were cytoplasmic in control conditions but became nuclear in Dox conditions.
claims.evidence: This is supported by subcellular fractionation and immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 5b.

claims.claim: STAT6 was nuclear in both control and doxycycline conditions.
claims.source: STAT6 was nuclear in both conditions.
claims.evidence: This is supported by subcellular fractionation and immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 5b.

claims.claim: Primary SFT tumor cells showed strong nuclear staining for NAB2 and STAT6.
claims.source: We first examined the primary tumor cells that we profiled by ChIP-seq (Figure 4) and retrieved a robust nuclear signal for NAB2 and STAT6 (Figure 5c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry shown in Figure 5c.

claims.claim: In wild-type U2OS conditions, NAB2 localization is largely cytoplasmic, while STAT6 signal is mostly nuclear.
claims.source: Next, we performed ICC in the U2OS inducible clone and confirmed that in wild-type conditions, NAB2 localization is largely cytoplasmic, while STAT6 signal is mostly nuclear (Figure 5c, Figure 5—figure supplement 1g).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry shown in Figure 5c and Figure 5—figure supplement 1g.

claims.claim: Upon NAB2-STAT6 expression, NAB2 and STAT6 signals co-localize in the nucleus.
claims.source: Upon NAB2-STAT6 expression, NAB2 and STAT6 signals co-localize in the nucleus, while a small amount of endogenous NAB2 remains cytoplasmic.
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry shown in Figure 5c.

claims.claim: NAB1 under physiological conditions is predominantly cytoplasmic.
claims.source: Accordingly, NAB1 under physiological conditions is predominantly cytoplasmic (Figure 5d, Figure 5—figure supplement 1h) and is redirected to the nucleus by NAB2-STAT6 (Figure 5d), having a similar fate to that of endogenous NAB2 (Figure 5b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry shown in Figure 5d and Figure 5—figure supplement 1h.

claims.claim: NAB1 is redirected to the nucleus by NAB2-STAT6.
claims.source: Accordingly, NAB1 under physiological conditions is predominantly cytoplasmic (Figure 5d, Figure 5—figure supplement 1h) and is redirected to the nucleus by NAB2-STAT6 (Figure 5d), having a similar fate to that of endogenous NAB2 (Figure 5b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunocytochemistry shown in Figure 5d.

claims.claim: About 30% of TCGA tumors had a positive ssGSEA score for the SFT gene signature.
claims.source: About 30% of TCGA tumors, including most sarcoma subtypes, had a positive ssGSEA score indicating that a significant number of EGR1-driven genes are upregulated (Figure 6a).
claims.evidence: This is supported by single-sample GSEA analysis across TCGA database shown in Figure 6a.

claims.claim: A group of neuroendocrine tumors (glioblastoma, mixed glioma, neuroblastoma, and pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma) were the most closely correlated to SFTs.
claims.source: Strikingly, a group of neuroendocrine tumors (glioblastoma, mixed glioma, neuroblastoma, and pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma) stood out as the most closely correlated to SFTs (Figure 6a).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ssGSEA analysis across TCGA database shown in Figure 6a.

claims.claim: Myeloid and lymphoid malignancies showed the poorest correlation to SFTs.
claims.source: Conversely, myeloid and lymphoid malignancies showed the poorest correlation (Figure 6a).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ssGSEA analysis across TCGA database shown in Figure 6a.

claims.claim: SFT-like tumors showed significantly worse outcomes in survival analysis.
claims.source: SFT-like tumors showed significantly worse outcomes, suggesting that expression of an EGR1 gene signature underlies tumor aggressiveness and/or therapy resistance (Figure 6b).
claims.evidence: This is supported by survival analysis across TCGA samples shown in Figure 6b.

claims.claim: One patient in the TCGA mesothelioma cohort (SH-A7BH) presented an outlier ssGSEA positive score.
claims.source: We, therefore, analyzed all transcriptomes from the TCGA collection of 87 mesotheliomas and identified one patient presenting an outlier ssGSEA positive score (Figure 6c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ssGSEA analysis of TCGA mesotheliomas shown in Figure 6c.

claims.claim: TCGA sample SH-A7BH was the only tumor in the mesothelioma cohort containing a NAB2-STAT6 fusion.
claims.source: We used Arriba to confirm that SH-A7BH was, in fact, the only tumor in the mesothelioma cohort containing a NAB2-STAT6 fusion (exons 1–6 of NAB2 and 16–22 of STAT6, Figure 6d).
claims.evidence: This is supported by fusion detection analysis using Arriba shown in Figure 6d.

claims.claim: The Homeobox domain was the most significantly enriched protein domain within the top 400 genes of the SFT signature.
claims.source: We resolved to examine the protein domains that were enriched within the top 400 genes of the SFT signature using the functional annotation tool InterPro. The most significantly enriched domain was the Homeobox domain (Figure 6e), which functions as a DNA-binding domain for a large class of transcription factors that are expressed during embryonic and fetal development to drive pattern formation, axis specification, ultimately leading to proper tissue and organ morphogenesis.
claims.evidence: This is supported by InterPro domain analysis shown in Figure 6e.

claims.claim: Several homeodomain transcription factors were overexpressed in SFTs (ALX4, SHOX2, SIX1).
claims.source: Notably, several homeodomain transcription factors were overexpressed in SFTs (ALX4, SHOX2, SIX1) and entire HOX clusters (HOXA, HOXC) were upregulated, as further confirmed by RNAPII profiling of a primary tumor tissue (Figure 6f).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq and RNAPII ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6f.

claims.claim: Entire HOX clusters (HOXA, HOXC) were upregulated in SFTs.
claims.source: Notably, several homeodomain transcription factors were overexpressed in SFTs (ALX4, SHOX2, SIX1) and entire HOX clusters (HOXA, HOXC) were upregulated, as further confirmed by RNAPII profiling of a primary tumor tissue (Figure 6f).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq and RNAPII ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6f.

claims.claim: RNAPII-bound enhancers (excluding NAB2-STAT6 targeted enhancers) showed overwhelming enrichment for homeotic proteins and Nanog.
claims.source: We then searched for enriched TF binding sites using all RNAPII-bound enhancers (excluding NAB2-STAT6 targeted enhancers) and found an overwhelming enrichment for homeotic proteins as well as Nanog (Figure 6g).
claims.evidence: This is supported by HOMER motif analysis of RNAPII enhancer peaks shown in Figure 6g.

claims.claim: SFTs correlated best with several neuronal tissue types in the Human Protein Atlas.
claims.source: SFTs correlated best with several neuronal tissue types and were the least correlated with lung and gut tissues (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Spearman correlation analysis with Human Protein Atlas RNA-seq datasets shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: SFTs were the least correlated with lung and gut tissues in the Human Protein Atlas.
claims.source: SFTs correlated best with several neuronal tissue types and were the least correlated with lung and gut tissues (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Spearman correlation analysis with Human Protein Atlas RNA-seq datasets shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The inversion on the long arm of chromosome 12 results in a gene fusion between NAB2 and STAT6.
claims.source: However, an intrachromosomal inversion on chromosome 12 was identified as the molecular hallmark of SFTs in 2013 (Robinson et al., 2013; Chmielecki et al., 2013). The inversion on the long arm of chromosome 12 results in a gene fusion between NAB2 and STAT6.
claims.evidence: This is a well-established molecular characteristic supported by prior research cited in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Immunohistochemistry using antibodies targeting the C-terminus of STAT6 reveals strong nuclear staining in the presence of the chimeric protein NAB2-STAT6.
claims.source: Immunohistochemistry using antibodies targeting the C-terminus of STAT6 reveals strong nuclear staining in the presence of the chimeric protein NAB2-STAT6, leading to STAT6 nuclear staining as a diagnostic tool for SFTs (Schweizer et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is a well-established diagnostic method supported by prior research.

claims.claim: Hemangiopericytomas are now classified as SFTs upon discovery of the NAB2-STAT6 gene fusion.
claims.source: Hemangiopericytomas were previously diagnosed as a distinct soft tissue neoplasm and upon discovery of the NAB2-STAT6 gene fusion, are now classified as SFTs (Bansal et al., 2021; Gengler and Guillou, 2006).
claims.evidence: This is a reclassification based on molecular findings, supported by citations.

claims.claim: STAT6 is a DNA-binding transcription factor operating downstream to the JAK/STAT signaling pathway in leukocytes.
claims.source: STAT6 is a DNA-binding transcription factor operating downstream to the JAK/STAT signaling pathway in leukocytes. STAT6 is commonly activated by cytokines such as IL-4 and IL-13 and mediates key immunological processes such as macrophage polarization and T-cell/B-cell activation (Vahedi et al., 2012; Czimmerer et al., 2018; Shimoda et al., 1996).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about STAT6 function supported by citations.

claims.claim: Activation of STAT6 occurs via JAK-mediated phosphorylation at Y641, triggering homodimerization via the SH2 domain and ultimately leading to nuclear translocation.
claims.source: Activation of STAT6 occurs via JAK-mediated phosphorylation at Y641, triggering homodimerization via the SH2 domain and ultimately leading to nuclear translocation (Hou et al., 1994; Takeda et al., 1996).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about STAT6 activation mechanism supported by citations.

claims.claim: Nuclear STAT6 stimulates transcription through its transactivation domain that recruits RNA Helicase A (RHA), SND1, and p300/CBP.
claims.source: Nuclear STAT6 stimulates transcription through its transactivation domain that recruits RNA Helicase A (RHA), SND1, and p300/CBP (Litterst and Pfitzner, 2001; Wang et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2002; Välineva et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about STAT6 transcriptional mechanism supported by citations.

claims.claim: NAB2 was originally characterized as a co-repressor of the Early Growth Response transcription factors (EGR1/2).
claims.source: Conversely, the NGFI-A binding protein 2 (NAB2) is expressed in most tissues and was originally characterized as a co-repressor of the Early Growth Response transcription factors (EGR1/2) (Svaren et al., 1996).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about NAB2 function supported by citation.

claims.claim: EGR1 is considered a broad regulator of cell proliferation and peaks during developmental processes.
claims.source: In fact, EGR1/2 are considered, like AP-1, broad regulators of cell proliferation and peak during developmental processes (Thiel and Cibelli, 2002).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about EGR1 function supported by citation.

claims.claim: EGR1 can modulate the expression of growth factors, such as IGF2 and TGF-β1, as well as that of NAB2.
claims.source: EGR1 can modulate the expression of growth factors, such as IGF2 and TGF-β1, as well as that of NAB2, and is believed to act either as an oncogene or tumor suppressor depending on the cellular context (Saha et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2021; Bae et al., 1999; de Belle et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about EGR1 targets supported by citations.

claims.claim: NAB2 forms homodimers and heterodimerizes with its family member NAB1.
claims.source: NAB2 forms homodimers and heterodimerizes with its family member NAB1, which was also described as a co-repressor of EGR1-dependent transcription (Svaren et al., 1998).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about NAB2 protein interactions supported by citation.

claims.claim: NAB2 may also function as co-activator of transcriptional enhancers during myeloid differentiation.
claims.source: We recently demonstrated that NAB2 may also function as co-activator of transcriptional enhancers during myeloid differentiation (Barbieri et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from prior work by the authors, supported by citation.

claims.claim: Most tumors (40–70%, especially those of pleural origin) carry a large fusion product of ~140 Kda resulting from exons 1–4 of NAB2 and exons 2–22 of STAT6.
claims.source: Most tumors (40–70%, especially those of pleural origin) carry a large fusion product of ~140 Kda resulting from exons 1–4 of NAB2 (retaining a truncated NCD2 domain and missing the C-terminal CID domain) and exons 2–22 of STAT6 (with the entire CDS).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about NAB2-STAT6 isoforms, likely supported by prior literature.

claims.claim: Another frequent NAB2-STAT6 isoform retains exons 1-5/6 of NAB2 and exons 16/17–22 of STAT6 and accounts for 10–20% of cases.
claims.source: Another frequent isoform retains a larger NAB2 moiety (exon 1-5/6, to include a truncated CID domain) and a much smaller STAT6 moiety (exon 16/17–22, missing the SH2 and DNA binding domains but retaining the transactivation domain). This shorter isoform accounts for 10–20% of cases and is most common in SFTs originating in extra-pleural locations.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about NAB2-STAT6 isoforms, likely supported by prior literature.

claims.claim: Risk of malignant progression, recurrence, and metastasis are not preferentially associated with either isoform of NAB2-STAT6.
claims.source: Risk of malignant progression, recurrence, and metastasis are not preferentially associated with either isoform of NAB2-STAT6 (Bieg et al., 2021; Park et al., 2019; Tai et al., 2015; Yuzawa et al., 2016; Chuang et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about NAB2-STAT6 isoforms and clinical outcomes, supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: The current risk assessment model (Demicco score) does not incorporate any molecular or genetic features of the primary tumor.
claims.source: In fact, the current risk assessment model (Demicco score) does not incorporate any molecular or genetic features of the primary tumor (Demicco et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about SFT risk assessment, supported by citation.

claims.claim: The mechanism of transcription activation by NAB2-STAT6 is conserved, whereas the targets are cell-type specific.
claims.source: We found limited overlap between NAB2-STAT6 sites in the primary tumor and those retrieved in U2OS (Figure 4e-f, Figure 4—figure supplement 1g-h), consistent with the limited overlap between their transcriptomes. It is likely that the mechanism of transcription activation by NAB2-STAT6 is conserved, whereas the targets are cell-type specific.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of limited overlap in binding sites but similar mechanisms.

claims.claim: The fusion protein utilizes the full EGR1 regulatory axis, including homo- and heterodimerization with NAB1/NAB2, to drive a highly distinctive transcriptional program.
claims.source: We further show that NAB2 is primarily contained in the cytoplasm and becomes nuclear-bound when fused to STAT6. The fusion protein utilizes the full EGR1 regulatory axis, including homo- and heterodimerization with NAB1/NAB2, to drive a highly distinctive transcriptional program that sets SFTs apart from most other tumors of mesenchymal origin.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on multiple lines of experimental evidence including IP-MS, ChIP-seq, and localization studies.

claims.claim: NAB2/NAB1 are co-activators of EGR-1 targets under physiological conditions, however, cytoplasmic localization restrains their activity.
claims.source: Our data suggest that the NAB2 moiety of the fusion protein targets a specific set of EGR1-dependent enhancers and proximal promoter sites and uses NAB1, or endogenous NAB2, as co-activators. In fact, our data suggest that NAB2/NAB1 are co-activators of EGR-1 targets under physiological conditions, however, cytoplasmic localization restrains their activity.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that NAB2/NAB1 are cytoplasmic in normal conditions but become nuclear and co-activate with NAB2-STAT6.

claims.claim: The NAB2 moiety of NAB2-STAT6 does not appear to recruit Integrator subunits.
claims.source: In myeloid cells, we found that full-length NAB2 recruits the Integrator protein complex. The NAB2 moiety of NAB2-STAT6 does not appear to recruit Integrator subunits, yet retains co-activator abilities by partnering with chromatin modifiers (CBP/P300) and helicases (RHA).
claims.evidence: This is based on comparison with prior work and IP-MS data showing recruitment of CBP/P300 and RHA but not Integrator.

claims.claim: SFTs upregulate secreted metabolic regulators such as CTRP11, neuropeptides and their activating enzymes (NPW, PCSK2), and chemokines/cytokines such as PDGFD, NTN3, DEFB136.
claims.source: In addition to IGF2 and IGF1 hormones, as we previously described, SFTs upregulate secreted metabolic regulators such as CTRP11, neuropeptides and their activating enzymes (NPW, PCSK2), and chemokines/cytokines such as PDGFD, NTN3, DEFB136 (Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data from primary tumors listed in Supplementary file 1.

claims.claim: Expression of an EGR1 gene signature underlies tumor aggressiveness and/or therapy resistance.
claims.source: SFT-like tumors showed significantly worse outcomes, suggesting that expression of an EGR1 gene signature underlies tumor aggressiveness and/or therapy resistance (Figure 6b).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on survival analysis showing worse outcomes for tumors with high SFT signature scores.

claims.claim: SFTs may originate from a corrupted developmental process from embryogenesis or fetal development.
claims.source: SFTs appear to upregulate an overwhelming number of homeotic transcription factors, as we showed, perhaps suggesting that the tumor mass may originate from a corrupted developmental process from embryogenesis or fetal development.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the upregulation of developmental transcription factors.

claims.claim: The primary SFT tumor used for ChIP-seq expressed the short isoform of NAB2-STAT6 containing exons 1–6 of NAB2 and exons 17–22 of STAT6.
claims.source: We obtained a fresh primary pre-sacral SFT post-surgery (no radiation or chemotherapy had been administered to the patient). This tumor expressed the short isoform of NAB2-STAT6 containing exons 1–6 of NAB2 and exons 17–22 of STAT6 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a).
claims.evidence: This is supported by fusion detection analysis using Arriba shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a.

claims.claim: The oncogenic NAB2-STAT6 fusion may reinforce its own expression in SFTs.
claims.source: Interestingly, NAB2 appeared upregulated in both systems as either the fusion protein or endogenous NAB2 bound the proximal promoter region (Figure 4f), furthermore, nucleosome accessibility and EGR1 binding increased in U2OS cells upon doxycycline treatment (Figure 4f). The oncogenic NAB2-STAT6 fusion may thereby reinforce its own expression in SFTs.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that NAB2-STAT6 binds to the NAB2 promoter and NAB2 expression increases.

claims.claim: SFTs are traditionally assimilated to soft tissue sarcomas and are often positive to CD34 staining.
claims.source: SFTs are traditionally assimilated to soft tissue sarcomas and are often positive to CD34 staining. They are broadly classified as mesenchymal tumors based on their histological patterns, albeit their cell of origin remains uncertain (Jo and Demicco, 2022).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about SFT classification supported by citation.

claims.claim: The cell of origin of SFTs remains uncertain.
claims.source: They are broadly classified as mesenchymal tumors based on their histological patterns, albeit their cell of origin remains uncertain (Jo and Demicco, 2022).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about the uncertainty of SFT cell of origin, supported by citation.

claims.claim: IGF2 was recognized as a major driver of a hypoglycemic condition occurring in <5% of SFTs (Doege-Potter syndrome).
claims.source: Notably, the most upregulated gene was IGF2, an EGR1 target that was recognized as a major driver of a hypoglycemic condition occurring in <5% of SFTs (Doege-Potter syndrome).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about IGF2's role in Doege-Potter syndrome.

claims.claim: SFTs may be immunologically 'cold'.
claims.source: Conversely, immune and cell signaling pathways are significantly downregulated (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d–e), suggesting that SFTs may be immunologically 'cold'.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the downregulation of immune pathways in RNA-seq data.

claims.claim: An EGR1-bound neuronal transcriptional program is being activated in SFT cells.
claims.source: These results suggest that an EGR1-bound neuronal transcriptional program is being activated in SFT cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the enrichment of EGR1 motifs at upregulated genes and the neuronal nature of these genes.

claims.claim: The primary function of NAB2-STAT6 may be transcriptional activation.
claims.source: About 27% of differentially expressed genes were downregulated (Figure 2c and Supplementary file 2), indicating that the primary function of NAB2-STAT6 may be transcriptional activation.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that most differentially expressed genes are upregulated rather than downregulated.

claims.claim: The fusion protein enables a feed-forward mechanism of the EGR1 regulatory axis.
claims.source: Interestingly, the expression of endogenous NAB2, NAB1, and EGR1 followed a similar trend, suggesting that the fusion protein enables a feed-forward mechanism of the EGR1 regulatory axis (Figure 2f).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that NAB2, NAB1, and EGR1 expression increases over time with NAB2-STAT6 expression.

claims.claim: NAB2-STAT6 does not possess any co-repressor activity and is instead functioning as a co-activator.
claims.source: NAB2 has been proposed to repress its own expression and that of NAB1 and EGR1. However, this trend suggests that NAB2-STAT6 does not possess any co-repressor activity and is instead functioning as a co-activator.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that NAB2, NAB1, and EGR1 are upregulated rather than repressed.

claims.claim: U2OS cells can be utilized to model the activity of the fusion protein but do not accurately represent the cell of origin of SFTs.
claims.source: The GO and TF enrichment analyses in U2OS cells closely matched our findings from primary SFTs (Figure 1), despite a limited overlap between the gene lists (15%, Figure 2—figure supplement 1d). Key EGR-1 targets such as IGF2 or the neuronal development regulators LHX2 and ROBO2 were commonly upregulated, indicating that U2OS cells can be utilized to model the activity of the fusion protein but do not accurately represent the cell of origin of SFTs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the similarity in mechanisms but differences in specific targets between U2OS and primary tumors.

claims.claim: NAB2-STAT6 localizes to EGR1 targets increasing their accessibility and expression.
claims.source: Collectively, these results demonstrate that NAB2-STAT6 localizes to EGR1 targets increasing their accessibility and expression.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, and RNA-seq data showing co-localization, increased accessibility, and increased expression.

claims.claim: NAB2-STAT6 localization is exclusively driven by EGR1 binding.
claims.source: Collectively, these findings align with data obtained in U2OS cells and suggest that NAB2-STAT6 localization is exclusively driven by EGR1 binding.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the enrichment of EGR1 motifs at NAB2-STAT6 peaks and the absence of STAT motifs.

claims.claim: A heterodimeric form of the oncogenic protein may be its most common form.
claims.source: NAB1 is the strongest interactor of NAB2-STAT6 across multiple experiments (Figure 5—figure supplement 1d), suggesting that a heterodimeric form of the oncogenic protein may be its most common form.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the strong and consistent interaction between NAB2-STAT6 and NAB1.

claims.claim: NAB2-STAT6 co-opts EGR1 co-activator functions.
claims.source: In addition, EGR1 co-purified along with CBP/P300 and RNAPII subunits suggesting that NAB2-STAT6 co-opts EGR1 co-activator functions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the co-purification of EGR1 with transcriptional co-activators in the presence of NAB2-STAT6.

claims.claim: The STAT6 moiety does not endow the fusion protein with the ability to recognize a subset of STAT motifs.
claims.source: Unlike previously proposed (Schweizer et al., 2013), we find that the STAT6 moiety of the fusion is the major driver of its nuclear localization (Figure 7). STAT6, however, does not endow the fusion protein with the ability to recognize a subset of STAT motifs, but may recruit additional co-activators.
claims.evidence: This is based on the absence of STAT motifs at NAB2-STAT6 binding sites despite the presence of the STAT6 moiety.

claims.claim: STAT6 may recruit additional co-activators to the fusion protein.
claims.source: STAT6, however, does not endow the fusion protein with the ability to recognize a subset of STAT motifs, but may recruit additional co-activators.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the known function of STAT6 and the presence of co-activators like SND1 and RHA in the interactome.

results.result: The manuscript provides background information on SFTs, including their incidence (1/1,000,000 per year), recurrence rates (30-40%), lack of effective therapies, and the NAB2-STAT6 fusion as their molecular hallmark. These claims establish the clinical and molecular context for the study.
results.evaluation: These claims (C1-C4, C59-C61, C70-C73, C84-C86) are well-established facts about SFTs supported by multiple citations to prior literature. They provide necessary background context and are not primary findings of this study. The claims are consistent with established knowledge in the field.

results.result: The manuscript reviews established knowledge about STAT6 and NAB2 protein functions, including STAT6's role in JAK/STAT signaling and NAB2's characterization as an EGR1/2 co-repressor that can also function as a co-activator.
results.evaluation: These claims (C62-C69) summarize well-established molecular biology of STAT6 and NAB2 proteins, supported by appropriate citations. C69 references the authors' own prior work. These provide necessary molecular context for understanding the fusion protein's function.

results.result: RNA-seq analysis of eight primary SFT tumors versus matched normal tissue reveals that all tumors share a common NAB2-STAT6 isoform (exons 1-4 of NAB2, exons 2-22 of STAT6), with IGF2 as the most upregulated gene, broad upregulation of neuronal development programs, downregulation of immune pathways, and enrichment of EGR1 binding motifs at promoters of upregulated genes.
results.evaluation: Claims C10-C14 and C88 are directly supported by RNA-seq data from FFPE samples (Figure 1), fusion detection using Arriba, differential expression analysis, GO/GSEA analysis, and motif enrichment analysis. The data quality appears appropriate for FFPE samples, and the analytical approaches are standard. The conclusion that an EGR1-bound neuronal program is activated is a reasonable inference from the data.

results.result: In a doxycycline-inducible U2OS cell model, NAB2-STAT6 expression peaks at 48 hours and induces upregulation of 562 genes (73% of differentially expressed genes) enriched for EGR1 motifs but not STAT motifs. Expression of endogenous NAB2, NAB1, and EGR1 increases over time, suggesting a feed-forward mechanism and that NAB2-STAT6 functions primarily as a transcriptional activator rather than repressor.
results.evaluation: Claims C15-C20 and C89-C91 are supported by immunoblot (Figure 2a), 3' mRNA QuantSeq (Figure 2c-f), and motif analysis (Figure 2e). The inducible system provides temporal control, and the data show clear dose-dependent effects. The inference about feed-forward activation (C90) and lack of co-repressor activity (C91) are reasonable interpretations of the observed upregulation of NAB2, NAB1, and EGR1. However, the claim about 'primary function' (C89) is somewhat speculative as it's based on the ratio of up- vs downregulated genes without mechanistic validation.

results.result: U2OS cells can model NAB2-STAT6 activity but do not accurately represent the cell of origin of SFTs, as evidenced by limited overlap (15%) in differentially expressed genes between U2OS and primary tumors despite similar GO/TF enrichment patterns.
results.evaluation: Claim C92 is supported by comparison of gene lists and enrichment analyses between U2OS and primary SFT data (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d). The authors appropriately acknowledge the limitations of their model system while noting that key mechanistic features (EGR1 enrichment, neuronal gene activation) are conserved. This is an important caveat for interpreting the U2OS data.

results.result: ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq in U2OS cells reveal that NAB2-STAT6 binds 1394 genomic sites (57% promoters, 43% enhancers) that are enriched for EGR1/EGR2 motifs but not STAT motifs. At these sites, endogenous EGR1 binding and chromatin accessibility increase at least twofold upon NAB2-STAT6 expression, and genes near these sites are significantly upregulated.
results.evaluation: Claims C21-C28 and C93 are well-supported by ChIP-seq for NAB2-STAT6 FLAG, endogenous EGR1, NAB2, and STAT6, plus ATAC-seq data (Figure 3). The motif analysis using HOMER is appropriate, and GSEA shows correlation between binding and gene expression. The observation that endogenous NAB2 but not STAT6 localizes to NAB2-STAT6 peaks in control conditions (C25) and that NAB2-STAT6 doesn't bind STAT6 control sites (C26) strongly supports the conclusion that the fusion protein's localization is driven by the NAB2 moiety and EGR1 binding.

results.result: ChIP-seq in a primary SFT tumor identifies 718 putative NAB2-STAT6 binding sites (69% distal enhancers) by overlapping NAB2 and STAT6 peaks. These sites are enriched for EGR1/2 motifs, correlate with upregulated genes in SFTs, and show limited overlap with U2OS NAB2-STAT6 sites, suggesting conserved mechanisms but cell-type-specific targets.
results.evaluation: Claims C29-C34, C82, and C94 are supported by ChIP-seq data from a primary tumor (Figure 4). The dual-antibody strategy to identify fusion protein binding sites is clever and validated by showing minimal NAB2/STAT6 overlap in control U2OS cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1b). The motif analysis and GSEA support the functional relevance of these sites. The limited overlap with U2OS (C34) is appropriately interpreted as reflecting cell-type specificity while maintaining mechanistic conservation. However, the conclusion that localization is 'exclusively' driven by EGR1 (C94) may be overstated—'predominantly' would be more accurate.

results.result: IP-MS experiments reveal that NAB1 and EGR1 are the top interactors of NAB2-STAT6, with NAB1 being the strongest interactor across multiple experiments. EGR1 co-purifies with CBP/P300 and RNAPII subunits, suggesting NAB2-STAT6 co-opts EGR1 co-activator functions. The fusion protein can also heterodimerize with endogenous full-length NAB2.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C38 and C95-C96 are supported by LC-MS/MS analysis of immunoprecipitates using NAB2, STAT6, EGR1, and FLAG antibodies (Figure 5a, Figure 5—figure supplement 1). The data from multiple IP approaches (NAB2, STAT6, FLAG in U2OS and HEK293T) provide strong convergent evidence. The identification of peptides unique to full-length NAB2 (C38) is particularly convincing. The inference that NAB2-STAT6 'co-opts' EGR1 functions (C96) is reasonable given the co-purification data, though direct functional validation would strengthen this claim.

results.result: Subcellular fractionation and immunocytochemistry demonstrate that in physiological conditions, NAB2 and NAB1 are primarily cytoplasmic while STAT6 is nuclear. Upon NAB2-STAT6 expression, the fusion protein is exclusively nuclear and redirects endogenous NAB2, NAB1, and EGR1 to the nucleus.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C39-C41, C43-C46 are supported by subcellular fractionation/immunoblot (Figure 5b) and immunocytochemistry in both U2OS cells and primary SFT tumor cells (Figure 5c-d). The data clearly show the redistribution of normally cytoplasmic proteins to the nucleus upon NAB2-STAT6 expression. The use of both biochemical fractionation and imaging provides strong convergent evidence. The controls (GAPDH, Histone H3) are appropriate.

results.result: The STAT6 moiety is the major driver of NAB2-STAT6 nuclear localization, but does not endow the fusion protein with the ability to recognize STAT motifs.
results.evaluation: Claims C8 and C97 are supported by the observation that STAT6 is nuclear in control conditions while NAB2 is cytoplasmic (Figure 5b), and the fusion protein is fully nuclear. The lack of STAT motif enrichment at NAB2-STAT6 binding sites (Figures 3b, 4c) and absence of binding to STAT6 control sites (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c) strongly support C97. However, the claim that STAT6 is the 'major driver' (C8) is an inference—direct mutagenesis of nuclear localization signals would provide stronger evidence.

results.result: Primary SFT tumor cells show strong nuclear staining for both NAB2 and STAT6 by immunocytochemistry.
results.evaluation: Claim C42 is directly supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 5c. This validates that the nuclear localization observed in the U2OS model system also occurs in actual tumor cells.

results.result: NAB2-STAT6 operates as a transcriptional coactivator for EGR1 target enhancers and promoters by redirecting NAB1, NAB2, and EGR1 to the nucleus. Under physiological conditions, NAB2/NAB1 are co-activators of EGR1 targets, but cytoplasmic localization restrains their activity. The NAB2 moiety of the fusion protein does not recruit Integrator subunits but retains co-activator abilities through CBP/P300 and RHA.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C7, C76-C78 represent the central mechanistic model of the paper, integrating multiple lines of evidence: ChIP-seq showing EGR1 motif enrichment (C5), localization studies showing nuclear redistribution (C7), IP-MS showing protein interactions (C76-C78), and comparison with prior work on full-length NAB2 (C78). The model is well-supported by the data, though the claim that NAB2/NAB1 are co-activators 'under physiological conditions' (C77) is somewhat speculative since the data primarily show they become co-activators when brought to the nucleus by the fusion protein.

results.result: Single-sample GSEA across TCGA reveals that SFTs activate a neuroendocrine gene signature that correlates most strongly with neuroendocrine tumors (glioblastoma, neuroblastoma, pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma) and least with myeloid/lymphoid malignancies. This pattern is also observed in correlation with Human Protein Atlas neuronal tissues.
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C47-C49, C57-C58 are supported by ssGSEA analysis across TCGA (Figure 6a) and Spearman correlation with Human Protein Atlas data (Figure 6—figure supplement 1). The analysis is appropriate and the sample size is large (22,687 TCGA samples). This provides important context for understanding SFT biology and suggests they may be more similar to neuroendocrine tumors than to typical sarcomas. The correlation analysis is descriptive but informative.

results.result: Survival analysis across TCGA shows that tumors with high SFT gene signature scores have significantly worse outcomes, suggesting that EGR1 gene signature expression underlies tumor aggressiveness and/or therapy resistance.
results.evaluation: Claim C50 is supported by survival analysis (Figure 6b) showing statistically significant differences (p<0.0001). However, the mechanistic interpretation in C80 that the EGR1 signature 'underlies' aggressiveness/resistance is speculative. The correlation could reflect many factors, and causality is not established. The survival analysis is across diverse tumor types, not specifically SFTs, which limits interpretation. Additional validation in SFT-specific cohorts would strengthen this claim.

results.result: The SFT gene signature successfully identifies a misclassified SFT (sample SH-A7BH) within the TCGA mesothelioma cohort, which was confirmed to harbor a NAB2-STAT6 fusion by Arriba analysis.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C52 are supported by ssGSEA analysis (Figure 6c) and fusion detection (Figure 6d). This provides strong validation that the SFT gene signature is specific and can identify NAB2-STAT6-driven tumors even when misclassified. This is a nice demonstration of the signature's utility.

results.result: InterPro domain analysis reveals that the Homeobox domain is the most enriched protein domain in the top 400 SFT signature genes. Several homeodomain transcription factors (ALX4, SHOX2, SIX1) and entire HOX clusters (HOXA, HOXC) are upregulated in SFTs, with RNAPII-bound enhancers showing enrichment for homeotic protein and Nanog motifs. This suggests SFTs may originate from a corrupted developmental process.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C56 are supported by InterPro analysis (Figure 6e), RNA-seq and RNAPII ChIP-seq data (Figure 6f), and HOMER motif analysis (Figure 6g). The data clearly show upregulation of developmental transcription factors. However, the speculation that SFTs 'may originate from a corrupted developmental process' (C81) is highly speculative and not directly tested. The authors appropriately use cautious language ('perhaps suggesting'), but this remains a hypothesis requiring further investigation.

results.result: SFTs upregulate secreted metabolic regulators, neuropeptides, and chemokines/cytokines, and may be immunologically 'cold' based on downregulation of immune pathways.
results.evaluation: Claim C79 is supported by RNA-seq data (Supplementary file 1), and C87 is supported by GO/GSEA analysis showing downregulation of immune pathways (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d-e). The characterization of SFTs as 'immunologically cold' is an inference that could be validated with additional immune profiling, but is reasonable given the data.

results.result: The mechanism of transcription activation by NAB2-STAT6 is conserved across cell types, but the specific target genes are cell-type specific. The fusion protein may reinforce its own expression by binding to the NAB2 promoter.
results.evaluation: Claim C74 is a reasonable inference from the limited overlap in binding sites but similar mechanisms between U2OS and primary tumors. Claim C83 is supported by observation of NAB2-STAT6 binding to the NAB2 promoter with increased accessibility and EGR1 binding (Figure 4f). However, functional validation (e.g., by disrupting this binding) would strengthen the claim about self-reinforcement.

results.result: The STAT6 moiety may recruit additional co-activators to the fusion protein.
results.evaluation: Claim C98 is speculative, based on the known function of STAT6 and the presence of SND1 and RHA in the interactome. While SND1 is known to be recruited by STAT6, the data don't definitively show whether these co-activators are recruited via the STAT6 moiety or through other interactions. This would require domain deletion studies or other functional validation.

results.result: RNA-seq analysis of eight primary SFT tumors revealed a common NAB2-STAT6 fusion isoform (exons 1-4 of NAB2 and exons 2-22 of STAT6), with IGF2 as the most upregulated gene, broad upregulation of neuronal development programs, downregulation of immune pathways, and enrichment of EGR1 binding motifs at promoters of upregulated genes.
results.evaluation: The reviewers describe the study as 'rigorously executed' and providing 'compelling data regarding the molecular characterization' of SFTs. They explicitly acknowledge that the authors 'identify enrichment of EGR1/NAB2 (but not STAT6) sites' and note the transcriptomic characterization without raising concerns about these primary tumor findings.

results.result: NAB2-STAT6 operates as a transcriptional coactivator targeting EGR1-bound enhancers and promoters. ChIP-seq and motif analysis in the U2OS inducible model showed overwhelming enrichment of EGR1 motifs but not STAT motifs at NAB2-STAT6 binding sites, with strong correlation between ChIP-seq targets and upregulated genes by RNA-seq.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state that the authors 'identify enrichment of EGR1/NAB2 (but not STAT6) sites bound by the fusion protein and increased expression of EGR1 targets.' This core mechanistic finding is highlighted as a key contribution without any critique, indicating reviewer acceptance of the coactivator function and EGR1-dependent binding mechanism.

results.result: In the U2OS inducible model, NAB2-STAT6 binds 1394 genomic sites (57% promoters, 43% distal regulatory regions) that show pre-existing EGR1 binding and moderate chromatin accessibility at baseline, with both EGR1 binding and accessibility increasing twofold upon NAB2-STAT6 expression. Endogenous NAB2, but not STAT6, localizes to these sites in control conditions, and NAB2-STAT6 does not bind STAT6 control sites.
results.evaluation: These detailed ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq findings are part of the 'detailed characterization of the transcriptomic and epigenomic NAB2-STAT6 SFT signatures' that reviewers describe as rigorous. The mechanistic data showing EGR1-dependent localization and chromatin changes are not questioned and support the overall model the reviewers endorse.

results.result: ChIP-seq analysis of a primary SFT tumor identified 718 putative NAB2-STAT6 binding sites (69% distal enhancers), with NAB2-only and NAB2-STAT6 sites enriched for EGR1/2 motifs while STAT6-only sites showed GRE and STAT motifs. Genes nearest to NAB2-STAT6 peaks were significantly upregulated in SFTs, suggesting NAB2-STAT6 localization is exclusively driven by EGR1 binding.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this as part of the 'detailed characterization' using 'primary tumor and adjacent normal tissue samples.' The finding that NAB2-STAT6 binding is EGR1-driven (not STAT6-driven) is explicitly mentioned by reviewers as a key discovery, indicating acceptance of these primary tumor ChIP-seq results.

results.result: NAB2-STAT6 redirects NAB1, NAB2, and EGR1 from cytoplasm to nucleus. In physiological conditions, NAB2 and NAB1 are predominantly cytoplasmic while STAT6 is nuclear. Upon NAB2-STAT6 expression, the fusion protein is exclusively nuclear and causes nuclear translocation of endogenous NAB2, NAB1, and EGR1. The STAT6 moiety is the major driver of nuclear localization.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state that 'Their studies indicate that NAB2-STAT6 fusion may direct the nuclear translocation of NAB2 and EGR1 proteins and potentially NAB1.' This direct acknowledgment of the subcellular localization findings indicates reviewer acceptance of these results from fractionation and immunocytochemistry experiments.

results.result: IP-MS analysis revealed NAB1 and EGR1 as top interactors of NAB2-STAT6 in nuclear extracts, with NAB1 being the strongest interactor across multiple experiments, suggesting a heterodimeric form may be most common. EGR1 co-purified with CBP/P300 and RNAPII subunits, suggesting NAB2-STAT6 co-opts EGR1 coactivator functions. The chimeric protein can also heterodimerize with endogenous full-length NAB2.
results.evaluation: These protein interaction findings are part of the mechanistic characterization that reviewers describe as 'rigorously executed.' The identification of NAB1 and EGR1 as key interactors supports the overall model of EGR1-dependent function that reviewers explicitly endorse, and no concerns are raised about the IP-MS methodology or conclusions.

results.result: NAB2-STAT6 activates a neuroendocrine gene signature that distinguishes SFTs from most sarcomas. TCGA analysis showed SFTs most closely correlate with neuroendocrine tumors (glioblastoma, neuroblastoma, pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma) and least with myeloid/lymphoid malignancies. Human Protein Atlas comparison confirmed strongest correlation with neuronal tissues and weakest with lung and gut tissues.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly note that 'Transcriptionally, NAB2-STAT6 SFTs most closely resemble neuroendocrine tumors,' directly acknowledging this key finding. This comparative analysis across tumor types is presented as an important contribution to understanding SFT biology without any critique.

results.result: The SFT gene signature is enriched for homeobox domain-containing transcription factors. Several homeodomain TFs (ALX4, SHOX2, SIX1) and entire HOX clusters (HOXA, HOXC) are upregulated in SFTs, confirmed by RNAPII ChIP-seq. RNAPII-bound enhancers (excluding NAB2-STAT6 sites) show overwhelming enrichment for homeotic protein and Nanog binding motifs.
results.evaluation: These findings are part of the transcriptomic characterization that reviewers describe as providing 'compelling data' and 'critical insight into the molecular pathogenesis of SFTs.' The developmental transcription factor signature is not questioned and contributes to the overall understanding of SFT biology that reviewers endorse.

results.result: In the U2OS inducible model, NAB2-STAT6 expression peaks at 48 hours of doxycycline treatment, leading to upregulation of 562 genes (73%) and downregulation of 211 genes (27%), suggesting transcriptional activation as the primary function. Expression of endogenous NAB2, NAB1, and EGR1 increases over time, suggesting a feed-forward mechanism of the EGR1 regulatory axis, indicating NAB2-STAT6 functions as a coactivator rather than corepressor.
results.evaluation: Reviewers describe the use of 'cells inducibly expressing NAB2-STAT6' as part of the rigorous experimental approach. The time-course data and inference about coactivator function are part of the mechanistic characterization that reviewers accept without critique, supporting the overall model of NAB2-STAT6 as an activator of EGR1 targets.

results.result: Survival analysis across TCGA samples showed that tumors with high SFT gene signature scores (SFT-like tumors) have significantly worse outcomes, suggesting that expression of an EGR1 gene signature underlies tumor aggressiveness and/or therapy resistance.
results.evaluation: This clinical correlation is part of the study's contribution to understanding SFT pathogenesis that reviewers describe as 'pivotal for the future development of mechanistically informed treatment approaches.' While speculative in mechanism, the survival association is presented as data-driven and is not questioned by reviewers.

results.result: Analysis of TCGA mesotheliomas identified one outlier patient (SH-A7BH) with a positive ssGSEA score for the SFT signature, which was confirmed by Arriba to be the only tumor in the cohort containing a NAB2-STAT6 fusion (exons 1-6 of NAB2 and 16-22 of STAT6).
results.evaluation: This case study demonstrates the utility of the SFT gene signature for identifying misclassified tumors and is part of the 'detailed characterization' that reviewers endorse. The fusion detection validates the signature's specificity and is not questioned.

results.result: There was limited overlap (15%) between NAB2-STAT6 binding sites and transcriptomes in primary tumors versus U2OS cells, suggesting the mechanism of transcription activation by NAB2-STAT6 is conserved while targets are cell-type specific. U2OS cells can model fusion protein activity but do not accurately represent the cell of origin of SFTs.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the use of both 'primary tumor and adjacent normal tissue samples and cells inducibly expressing NAB2-STAT6' without raising concerns about the limited overlap. The interpretation that mechanism is conserved while targets differ is consistent with the overall rigorous characterization that reviewers endorse.

results.result: The fusion protein utilizes the full EGR1 regulatory axis, including heterodimerization with NAB1/NAB2, to drive a distinctive transcriptional program. NAB2/NAB1 function as coactivators of EGR1 targets under physiological conditions, but cytoplasmic localization restrains their activity. The NAB2 moiety does not recruit Integrator subunits but retains coactivator abilities via CBP/P300 and RHA. The STAT6 moiety drives nuclear localization but does not confer STAT motif recognition, though it may recruit additional coactivators.
results.evaluation: These mechanistic conclusions synthesize multiple experimental findings that reviewers describe as providing 'critical insight into the molecular pathogenesis of SFTs.' The model of NAB2-STAT6 function is consistent with all the data reviewers explicitly endorse, and no concerns are raised about these interpretations.

results.result: Background claims about SFT epidemiology, clinical features, molecular hallmarks, and the known functions of NAB2, STAT6, and EGR1 proteins based on established literature and prior research.
results.evaluation: These are established background facts cited from literature that provide context for the study. Reviewers do not question any of these foundational claims, and they are standard knowledge in the field that frames the novel findings.

results.result: SFTs upregulate various secreted factors including metabolic regulators (CTRP11), neuropeptides (NPW, PCSK2), and chemokines/cytokines (PDGFD, NTN3, DEFB136). The primary tumor used for ChIP-seq expressed the short NAB2-STAT6 isoform (exons 1-6 of NAB2, 17-22 of STAT6). NAB2-STAT6 may reinforce its own expression by binding the NAB2 promoter.
results.evaluation: These are supporting observations from the transcriptomic and ChIP-seq analyses that reviewers describe as rigorous and detailed. While not highlighted as major findings, they are part of the comprehensive characterization that reviewers endorse without critique.

results.result: Speculative interpretations: SFTs may originate from a corrupted developmental process based on upregulation of homeotic transcription factors; SFTs may be immunologically 'cold' based on downregulation of immune pathways; an EGR1-bound neuronal transcriptional program is being activated in SFT cells.
results.evaluation: These are interpretive statements based on the data that reviewers describe as providing 'critical insight.' While speculative, they are reasonable inferences from the transcriptomic findings that reviewers accept as part of the overall contribution to understanding SFT biology. Reviewers note this work is 'a critical first step towards targeted precision medicine approaches,' implying acceptance of these mechanistic interpretations.

comparisons.comparison: Both strongly support the primary tumor RNA-seq findings (C10-C14). OpenEval provides detailed methodological assessment of RNA-seq, fusion detection, and differential expression analysis. Peer reviewers describe the study as 'rigorously executed' and explicitly acknowledge the EGR1 enrichment findings. OpenEval additionally evaluates C88 (EGR1-bound neuronal program) which peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of the rigorous characterization.

Both support the core mechanistic finding that NAB2-STAT6 binds EGR1 sites (not STAT6 sites) and acts as a coactivator. OpenEval evaluates detailed ChIP-seq claims (C21-C28, C93), while peer reviewers explicitly state authors 'identify enrichment of EGR1/NAB2 (but not STAT6) sites' and highlight this as a key contribution. OpenEval provides more granular assessment of individual experimental findings, while peer review offers broader endorsement of the mechanism.

Strong agreement on ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq data showing EGR1-dependent localization (C21-C26). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of the dual-antibody ChIP-seq strategy and motif analysis. Peer reviewers describe this as part of the 'detailed characterization of the transcriptomic and epigenomic NAB2-STAT6 SFT signatures' without raising concerns. Both accept the mechanistic conclusion that NAB2 moiety drives fusion protein localization.

Both support primary tumor ChIP-seq findings (C29-C33, C94). OpenEval notes the clever dual-antibody strategy and validates the EGR1-driven binding model, though suggests 'predominantly' rather than 'exclusively' for C94. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as part of the detailed characterization using primary tumor samples and endorse the EGR1-driven (not STAT6-driven) mechanism as a key discovery.

Strong agreement on nuclear translocation findings (C6, C39-C46). OpenEval details the convergent evidence from fractionation and immunocytochemistry in both U2OS and primary tumor cells. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'Their studies indicate that NAB2-STAT6 fusion may direct the nuclear translocation of NAB2 and EGR1 proteins and potentially NAB1,' directly acknowledging these subcellular localization results.

Perfect agreement on protein interaction findings (C35-C38, C95-C96). OpenEval assesses the IP-MS data showing NAB2-STAT6 co-purifies with EGR1 and NAB1, noting convergent evidence from multiple approaches. Peer reviewers describe this as part of the 'rigorously executed' mechanistic characterization supporting the EGR1-dependent function model. Both accept the conclusion that NAB2-STAT6 'co-opts' EGR1 functions.

Strong agreement on neuroendocrine similarity findings (C9, C48-C49, C57-C58). OpenEval evaluates the ssGSEA analysis across TCGA and correlation with Human Protein Atlas data as appropriate and informative.
